rationale: This ethnographic study examines the role of traveling trade shows in forming the US real-time computing market during the mid-1990s. It has no connection to household or community water or sanitation services, legal/administrative service-access rules, or water/sanitation access outcomes (E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both the narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings because the study is entirely unrelated to household or community water or sanitation service access (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: Specifically, the article studies the role of the traveling trade show in creating the real time computing market, which is part of the US electronics sector, during the mid-1990's.
By applying ethnographic methods, we explore the general question of how economic actors cope with uncertainty in the phase of market-making and at the cutting edge of technology.
